content:
Sergio Costa: metrics look off rn. seeing a p99 spike on Hosted /v1/chat in eu-west right after we flipped traffic. errors are mostly fine but latency jumped hard. is this clients retrying or routing doing something weird? :eyes:

Allison Grant: yep, seeing it too. panel: `failover_game_day/us-east->eu-west` p95 went from ~1.4s to ~4.8s for ~6-7 mins. 5xx burn didn’t move much, but 429s ticked up.

Miles Thornton: can someone sanity check it’s not just dashboard aggregation weirdness? are we looking at server-side duration vs client-perceived?

Sergio Costa: this is gateway `request_duration_seconds` (server-side) w/ route label = chat. also perf-canary latency is elevated but less dramatic.

Peter Holtz: if gateway duration spikes + 429s, could be retry storm. do we have `retry_after_sent` metric on the overload responses?

Allison Grant: checking… `api_gateway_overload_retry_after_total{region="eu-west"}` is basically flat. so not obviously the new retry-after behavior.

Mina Haddad: routing side: policy flip looked clean. `policy_engine_decision_total{action="shift_region", from="us-east", to="eu-west"}` matches the planned step. no extra flips.

Ravi Menon: any chance we’re hot-spotting a subset of eu-west pools? e.g. dedicated spillover or a bad weight on the route?

Vikram Singh: looking at `routing_backend_pick_rate` by cluster. eu-west is skewing to `ew1-gpu-pool-b` more than expected (like 78/22). not sure if that’s normal given current capacity.

Vanessa Ortiz: heads up: eu-west headroom is lower than baseline today; autoscaler is mid-scale. but shouldn’t cause a step-function p99 like that unless queueing.

Miles Thornton: queueing hypothesis: we might be hitting batcher saturation / KV cache warmup. do we have `inference_queue_time_ms` split by region?

Allison Grant: yep. `inference_queue_time_ms_p95` in eu-west jumped from ~40ms -> ~700ms during the spike window. that points to capacity/queueing vs networking.

Peter Holtz: could still be client retries causing extra load that pushes queueing. do we see `request_total` jump at the same time?

Sergio Costa: `api_gateway_requests_total{region="eu-west"}` increases as expected with the shift (obviously), but there’s an extra ~18-22% above the planned ramp for ~5 mins. that smells like retries.

Tomáš Novák: do we have breakdown of retry causes? if clients get redirects + timeouts, they might double-send.

Mina Haddad: redirect rate: `gateway_redirect_total` spiked as planned (we’re moving them). but after the flip, redirects should go down. they did.

Ravi Menon: are we sure streaming clients aren’t reconnecting and restarting the request? that was one of the known issues.

Peter Holtz: +1. if they treat redirect as failure and retry full payload, could inflate load and increase queueing.

Devon Price: incident-bot timeline has the failover event at T+0. we can correlate to client SDK logs? any sample from support?

Sergio Costa: no support pings yet (good). but we can check gateway logs for duplicate `idempotency_key` usage.

Allison Grant: quick log query (prod log explorer) for eu-west during spike window:
```
filter service="api-gateway" region="eu-west" route="/v1/chat" 
| stats count() as c, count_distinct(idempotency_key) as uniq by minute
```
Seeing c/uniq ratio creep from ~1.02 -> ~1.21 for a few minutes.

Miles Thornton: that’s pretty indicative. not definitive (idempotency_key is optional) but still.

Vikram Singh: also seeing elevated `upstream_connect_time_ms` on a subset of pods in `ew1-gpu-pool-b`. maybe pool-b has a networking issue? or just overloaded.

Vanessa Ortiz: pool-b currently has fewer healthy nodes (maintenance drain earlier). weights might be stale.

Mina Haddad: routing weights are pulled from capacity service every 30s w/ TTL jitter (post PR-19825). if capacity feed is stale or missing, could default. are we missing a signal?

Allison Grant: region-health logs show one warning: `capacity_headroom_signal missing for ew1-gpu-pool-a` around the same time. controller shouldn’t crash (we fixed NPE) but might degrade to conservative weights.

Ravi Menon: if pool-a capacity signal missing, policy engine may be biasing away from it and piling onto pool-b.

Peter Holtz: so two contributing things: (1) some clients retrying during redirect, (2) routing skew due to missing capacity signal.

Sergio Costa: can we confirm if latency spike aligns with skew? queue time spike matches when pick rate goes 78/22.

Vikram Singh: yep. at ~T+3min skew increases; p99 follows. at ~T+10min skew normalizes (55/45) and p99 recovers.

Miles Thornton: action items for now:
1) stabilize weights (ensure capacity signal feed for pool-a)
2) add a dashboard panel/alert for `missing_signal` so we don’t debug blind mid-gameday
3) follow up on streaming redirect retry behavior (ENG-2422?)

Allison Grant: +1. for the rest of the game day, suggest we pause next step until we confirm capacity signal is stable.

Incident Bot: Automated note: `failover_event` annotation added to dashboards (event_id=fo_1768613605_ew1). Links: https://grafana/redwood/d/failover-signals?var-region=eu-west

Tomáš Novák: go/no-go thread wants clear call. can someone post a short summary there? (suspect retries + routing skew due to missing capacity signal; recovered once signal returned).

Sergio Costa: I’ll post in go/no-go. also capturing timestamps: spike started ~1768613780, recovered ~1768614200.

Peter Holtz: any immediate mitigation if it happens again? could temporarily increase gateway timeouts? or cap retries?

Mina Haddad: safest is reduce skew by pinning weights 50/50 while capacity feed is flaky. I can do a scoped config override for game day tenant allowlist only.

Miles Thornton: do that. keep blast radius tiny. and let’s log it as a gameday issue + follow-up ticket for the capacity feed reliability + routing behavior when signal missing.

Devon Price: I’ll add to the incident timeline + create a follow-up in ENG-2426 tracker.

Allison Grant: also noting: perf-canary did NOT see the full spike, which supports the “client behavior” part (real users retrying more than canary). we should include in retro.

Sergio Costa: ok. summary: latency spike was real; queue time jumped; request volume above expected; idempotency duplication up; routing skewed to pool-b likely due to missing capacity headroom signal for pool-a. mitigations in progress.
